correspondence.component_scope: Eastern high icefield opening and descending western/southwestern glacial branch
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies within the mapped Chilkat Glacier icefield setting and follows its western/southwestern branch toward the ice-marginal foreland. The original topographic ice area and enclosed contours, with clear imagery of the glacial branch and its descending valley, establish ordinary geographic correspondence. The glacier label is bounded to the broader icefield setting, not treated as a river name or exact named-branch boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Ice-marginal pool/foreland, northwest glacier trough, border crossing and upper receiving basin
correspondence.finding: The selected route passes through a small ice-marginal pool/foreland and turns northwest along the main glacial trough. Clear imagery depicts the continuous trough, terminal debris/ice margin and receiving water basin across the border. It closes the Canadian transfer that the topographic source alone does not depict fully. Differences in mapped and photographed ice extent do not require present subglacial-hydraulic inference or a continuously wet channel on every position. No intervening separate basin is apparent at the ordinary geographic scale read.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper lake-like widening, westward Chilkat River, southward return across the border and southwest reach
correspondence.finding: The unnamed upper waterbody broadening opens west into a directly labeled Chilkat River channel. The selected route follows that river west and south across the international boundary, then southwest through confined reaches and broad water polygons. An eastern glacier-fed feeder joins below the border before the corridor reaches the western Tahini River junction. The upper waterbody retains a bounded unnamed lake-like status; the river label is not imposed as its natural-lake name.

correspondence.component_scope: Tahini receiving junction, southward Chilkat valley and Kelsall confluence
correspondence.finding: The mapped Chilkat continues through the Tahini joining setting and southward within its continuous valley/floodplain to the Kelsall confluence from the west. The selected generalized line stays in this ordinary receiving corridor, including river widenings and minor lateral tributaries. Tahini and Kelsall are separately bounded tributary names.

correspondence.component_scope: Braided Chilkat river-bottom corridor past side-water settings to the highway/Klukwan approach
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor continues through the braided Chilkat floodplain and wooded/wetland river-bottom settings, passing side lakes and unnamed tributary mouths before the highway crossing and the adjoining lower fragment. Nearby Mosquito Lake labels do not supply a mainstem name or imply a selected through-lake passage. Braided-thread and bank differences are ordinary cartographic generalization within one mapped receiving floor.

correspondence.component_scope: Continuous fragment join, Klehini confluence, Klukwan and Tsirku receiving floor
correspondence.finding: The lower fragment continues in the same Chilkat River near the Klehini joining corridor and Klukwan, then passes the Tsirku confluence and broad common river-bottom floor. Independent state-park prose corroborates the distinct Chilkat, Klehini/Kleheni and Tsirku river-bottom settings. Neither nearby Chilkat Lake nor Chilkoot Lake is a selected through-lake component.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Chilkat floodplain and Takhin confluence
correspondence.finding: The mapped lower Chilkat forms one continuous broad braided and wetland receiving corridor beside the valley road. The selection remains within that corridor past the distinct Takhin tributary joining from the west and onward toward the estuary. A named tributary label on the common lower water polygon does not make it an alias of the selected system.

correspondence.component_scope: Delta approach, marine-inlet extension, actual render ending and separate source endpoint
correspondence.finding: The last selected parts pass from the lower river/delta into the adjoining Chilkat Inlet receiving setting along the delta margin. The render ending is within this marine receiving setting; the distinct source endpoint is farther seaward in the same inlet. These two terminal descriptions are preserved separately. The final inlet extension is not claimed to be a wholly natural-river reach, and no exact contemporary mouth or tidal-waterline alignment is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Small northern lake edge and southwest headward feeder
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is at the small northern lake’s southern/southwestern edge. The detailed original exposes a southwest-trending shallow drainage swale through pale, rocky terrain into a confined bedrock stream corridor leading to the larger lake below. Small neighboring ponds and the separate northern/western approaches are distinguishable. The ordinary receiving corridor is established without requiring exact agreement with each coarse selected vertex or a continuously visible presently wet thread. No independent name is established for this feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: First elongated lake passage and rocky southern outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected route passes southwest through the first elongated lake, then through its rocky outlet and intervening smaller waterbody into the next lower receiving corridor. The detailed view and overlapping route overview expose the lake basin, confined outlet and ordinary joining geography. These northern lake components are left unnamed rather than extending Generator Lake’s name to every waterbody.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest succession of narrow waterbodies and connecting valley reaches
correspondence.finding: Successive narrow waterbodies and rocky interlake passages occupy a continuous southwest-trending depression east of the ice-margin terrain. Short side gullies join from the surrounding slopes. The route remains in this lake-and-channel chain and does not cross over the ice cap or shift to a separate neighboring basin. Seasonal snow/ice and mixed photographic epochs are not interpreted as present hydraulic conditions.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern and southern passage through the broad southwestern ice-margin lake
correspondence.finding: The narrow upper lake corridor opens into the broad southwestern lake basin. The selected passage follows its eastern side to the southeastern/southern outlet setting. The regulatory prose’s combination of Generator Lake, Barnes Ice Cap and the Clyde bank directly east supports this bounded lake identity. The glacier/ice cap is adjacent westward; no selected crossing over the ice itself is asserted, and no current ice-dam or calving behavior is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake outlet, eastern sediment corridor and turn toward the northeast
correspondence.finding: A connected eastward sediment-and-channel corridor leaves the large lake, passes small pools and gravel flats, and turns toward the northeast-trending receiving valley. The historical regulatory clauses explicitly connect the Clyde River bank to Generator Lake’s southern shore and identify a point on the same eastern river reach. Coarse selected segments fall across the wider valley/terrace setting; they do not require a new cross-basin transfer or a river name for each adjacent pool.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast-trending middle river, pools and tributary joins
correspondence.finding: The eastward lake-outlet corridor continues into the northeast valley through broader sediment reaches, confined rocky sections and local widenings. Side gullies and short lake-fed tributaries join the same receiving corridor. Adjacent dark and turquoise lakes are distinguished from the selected through-route; no reservoir, managed transfer or ice crossing is required by the observed geography.

correspondence.component_scope: Long northeast river continuation into the lower valley
correspondence.finding: The same river corridor can be followed through northeast-oriented bends, local narrows and flatter gravel reaches. The selected progression and successive tributary joins remain in one receiving valley; neighboring lake basins lie beside it. This geographic continuity connects the named Generator Lake outlet reach with the independently named coastal Clyde River.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower bends, southern tributary confluence and broad inlet-head delta
correspondence.finding: The lower valley bends eastward, receives a substantial southern approach, then turns northeast into a broad sandy/gravelly delta plain at the inlet head. Visible channels, bars and floodplain patches occupy the same continuous receiving setting. This directly matches the CHS description of Clyde River entering Kangiqtugaapik through a flat, bare sand-and-gravel expanse, independently distinguishing it from nearby side-fiord or tributary settings.

correspondence.component_scope: Separate stored source terminal and rendered terminal at the inlet-head delta margin
correspondence.finding: The actual selected ending lies at the southern/eastern margin of the river’s inlet-head delta. The stored source endpoint is at the coastal water-edge setting; the rendered endpoint is slightly southward/landward along the same delta-to-inlet margin. Both are accounted for separately. No exact present channel bank, surveyed river mouth or tidal waterline is asserted, and no unselected continuation down the long inlet to the settlement or open Baffin Bay is appended.

correspondence.component_scope: northern opening and initial tributary join
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening follows a narrow, branching upland drainage corridor southeast and then south. The image distinguishes the selected branch from neighboring gullies and shows the short southwestward continuation joining the wider receiving valley. No nearby feature name is assigned to the opening.

correspondence.component_scope: eastward receiving valley and turn
correspondence.finding: The selected route enters the broad pale valley floor, bends southeast and then east/northeast, passes a substantial northern tributary junction and continues east to the pronounced southern turn. The whole valley-floor connection is visible, including side-gully joins; the selected path is not treated as a precise bank trace.

correspondence.component_scope: southward upper trunk
correspondence.finding: After the eastern turn, a continuous south-running dry-valley corridor follows the upland margin. Successive tributary gullies join it, and the corridor continues to the southern elbow where it turns westward. Small neighboring cloud/shadow patches do not remove the visible ordinary valley connection.

correspondence.component_scope: southwestward middle canyon
correspondence.finding: The elbow continues west and southwest through an incised, locally green-toned canyon corridor, receiving side valleys before turning south. Overlapping original views account for the full middle connection and all three stored parts without an inferred ridge or separate-basin crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: middle southward and southeastward sequence
correspondence.finding: The receiving channel winds south between dissected hills, turns east and southeast around the adjoining uplands, and opens into a broader pale alluvial corridor. Side-canyon junctions and the final southward outlet from this terrain are visible throughout.

correspondence.component_scope: lower alluvial corridor and lake approach
correspondence.finding: The selected southward and southwestward succession follows the continuous alluvial floor below the hills, with a meandering dry channel and diffuse pale depositional surfaces. It reaches the northern receiving-lakebed approach at the foot of the western uplands. Local shadows reduce detail but not the valley-to-basin connection.

correspondence.component_scope: northern grande lakebed passage
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation enters the elongated northern lakebed tongue and follows its pale, locally darker central receiving floor southward into the broader Grande depression. DPA’s authorial lake account and processed multitemporal imagery identify this larger northern lake and distinguish it from Chica farther south. A continuous receiving lakebed establishes ordinary passage even where the photographed surface is dry.

correspondence.component_scope: actual terminal lakebed endpoint
